# iClock

> Ultra-lightweight (253 KB), zero-dependency Windows native productivity hub: transparent click-through countdown timer, ambient 0-polling daily quotes, 20+ AI agents monitor, and native stdio Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.

iClock is an open-source, minimalist Windows desktop productivity hub designed for developers and power users. It compiles to a single 253 KB native portable executable with zero runtime dependencies.

## Key Specifications

- **Application Category**: Desktop Utility, Focus & Pomodoro Countdown Timer, Daily Quotes, AI Agent Completion Monitor, MCP Server
- **Architecture**: Pure C# WinForms (.NET Framework 4.x runtime, built into Windows 10/11)
- **Binary Size**: ~253 KB single file, portable (no installation required)
- **Memory Footprint**: < 15 MB static RAM
- **Operating System Compatibility**: Windows 7 SP1, Windows 8, Windows 10, Windows 11
- **Display Mode**: Floating desktop text with native click-through (`WS_EX_TRANSPARENT`)
- **Global Hotkey**: Configurable system-wide toggle (default: `Ctrl+Shift+T`)
- **Default Appearance**: Font size 20 px, Red text (`#FF0000`)
- **Supported Formats**: `HH:MM:SS`, `MM:SS`, and localized time units (`00时25分00秒` / `00h 25m 00s`)
- **Built-in Native MCP Server**: `iclock.com --mcp` stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 (Zero Node.js/Python dependencies)
  - `iclock_ask_human`: Desktop Decision Gate (Human-in-the-Loop popup for agent safety authorization)
  - `iclock_progress`: Ghost Progress Meter (2px hairline capsule on bottom of floating clock)
  - `iclock_timer`: Agent sets, queries, and controls countdown timers
  - `iclock_notify`: Agent triggers desktop top-most popups and chimes upon task milestones
  - `iclock_quote`: Agent reads or rotates desktop motivational quotes
  - `iclock_status`: Agent queries runtime system and timer status
- **Ambient Daily Quotes**: 0-Polling event-driven hibernation (0.0% CPU idle), 300+ bilingual library, AI/MCP batch expansion with automatic deduplication and `quotes.txt.bak` backup
- **License**: MIT License (100% free and open-source)
- **Author & Maintainer**: gujiangwen (francodeyvison183@gmail.com)
- **Privacy & Safety**: 0 Ads, zero bundled software, zero background telemetry

## Download & Installation

- **Windows Package Manager (WinGet)**:
  ```powershell
  winget install FrancoDeyvison.iClock
  ```
- **Scoop Package Manager**:
  ```powershell
  scoop install https://raw.githubusercontent.com/francodeyvison183-collab/iClock/main/scoop/iclock.json
  ```
- **Official Website**: https://francodeyvison183-collab.github.io/iClock/
- **GitHub Repository**: https://github.com/francodeyvison183-collab/iClock

## Core Differentiators

1. **Native Lightweight vs Electron Bloat**: While typical modern desktop timers consume 150 MB~400 MB of RAM with hundreds of megabytes in download size, iClock requires only ~253 KB on disk and less than 15 MB of RAM.
2. **True TopMost & Click-Through**: Remains visible over full-screen IDEs, games, or presentation software without capturing or blocking mouse clicks (`WS_EX_TRANSPARENT`).
3. **Native Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server**: Provides native Windows stdio MCP server for Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, and Antigravity, introducing `iclock_ask_human` for critical desktop human-in-the-loop authorization.
4. **AI Agent Background Collaboration**: Monitors 20+ domestic and international AI coding agents (Cursor, Antigravity, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Trae, Tongyi Lingma, CodeGeeX, MiniMax, CodeBuddy, etc.) via a 4-tier perception engine (Toast, Win32 Shell taskbar flash at 0ms, window title state badge, and edge-detected cluster CPU fallback) with instant alert and 1-click window restore.
5. **0-Polling Ambient Desktop Quotes**: Floats on desktop with direct micro-interactions (Alt+drag move, right edge width resize, Alt+Ctrl+wheel font scale), consuming 0.0% CPU when idle.
6. **Command Line & IPC Automation**: Built-in 0ms Win32 `WM_COPYDATA` pipeline supporting terminal controls (`iclock -s 25`, `-p`, `-r`, `--reset`, `-n <msg>`) and script automation without `.exe` via `--install-cli`.
7. **Daily Focus History**: Right-click the system tray to review completed, reset, or interrupted countdown records for the day.
